source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ Χριστιανοὺς ἐγκαταλείπειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ ἀπιέναι, καὶ ἀγγέλους ὀνομάζειν, καὶ συνάξεις ποιεῖν, ἅπερ ἀπηγόρευται. Εἴ τις οὖν εὐρεθῇ ταύτῃ κεκρυμμένῃ εἰδωλολατρείᾳ σχολάζων, ἔστω ἀνάθεμα, ὅτι ἐγκατέλιπε τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ εἰδωλολατρείᾳ προσῆλθεν.
thought_title: Against secret idolatry and angel assemblies
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its decrees; this canon forbids Christians from leaving the church to name angels and hold assemblies, and curses anyone found practicing such hidden idolatry.
pass_a_gloss: That not [it] is necessary [for] Christians to abandon the assembly of God, and to go away, and angels to name, and gatherings to make, which things have been forbidden. If anyone therefore should be found in this hidden idolatry devoting himself, let him be anathema, because he abandoned the Lord of us Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and to idolatry he came near.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the infinitive phrase; the canon forbids invoking or naming angels in assemblies, and 'name' preserves the exact verb.
Literal for 'make assemblies'; 'hold' is the natural English verb for convening gatherings while keeping the noun 'assemblies'.
The perfect passive participle 'hidden' modifies 'idolatry'; the canon condemns secret idolatrous practice, so the adjective is kept literal.
The participle means 'having leisure for' or 'being occupied with'; 'devoting himself to' captures the ongoing engagement with the hidden idolatry.
The verb means 'came to' or 'approached'; 'went over to' conveys the defection to idolatry in contrast with abandoning Christ.

pass_b_english: Christians must not abandon the church of God and go away to invoke angels and hold assemblies, which has been forbidden. If anyone is found devoting himself to this hidden idolatry, let him be accursed, because he has abandoned our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and gone over to idolatry.

problems.why: ὀνομάζειν here means 'invoke/call upon by name,' not merely 'name.'
problems.ruling: ὀνομάζειν in this context means 'invoke/call upon,' not bare 'name'; 'name angels' misleads readers about the cultic practice.

fixed: Changed 'name angels' to 'invoke angels' because ὀνομάζειν here means 'invoke/call upon by name,' not merely 'name.'
